chunks: And in it, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who follow him.
And He made for them partners in it to mislead them from what was brought to them.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this verse to clarify that Satan's dominion is not coercive but relies on human consent, a key tenet in Shia theology regarding free will. The mention of 'partners' (shuraka) refers to the false deities or worldly attachments that believers may adopt, thereby granting Satan authority over them through their own choices.
